newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin Thanong sees economy bottoming out.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin Thanong sees economy bottoming out.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said the country's economic downturn may have begun bottoming out with some signs of recovery in certain sectors.
"Our economy has nearly bottomed out. Some sectors have already began to recover," he told reporters late on Sunday on his return from Japan after a brief visit.
He did not specify the sectors which were improving.

Thailand's economic growth this year was expected to be around four percent, which is still better than some other countries, Thanong said. Some private economists have put growth at up to three percent for this year as the country weathers its worst economic slump in over a decade.
"The slower economic growth to around four percent from 6.7 percent last year is acceptable. We want the economic growth to go along with stability," he said.

The finance minister reiterated what he said in Tokyo -- that he had asked Japanese creditors to restructure their short-term loans granted to Thai borrowers into long-term ones to reduce the debt payment burden of domestic businesses.
Japan's government and the private sector had responded positively to his request, he said.
He repeated that Thailand had not asked for financial support from Japan during his visit.
But Thailand and Japan had agreed to cooperate to promote stability in currency markets including intervention to help the baht if the currency faced renewed speculative attacks, he said.
"The stability of the baht is vital to the economy of Thailand and other countries in the region," he said.

The Thai baht and the Philippine pesos were effectively devalued this month following repeated speculative assaults. Thailand allowed a managed float of its embattled baht on July 2 which resulted in a loss of about 15 percent in the value of the currency.
